title: Session run log - micro experiments
content:
Session run log — quick scratchsheet (personal)

Owner: Lucas Patel
Date range: 2026-02-25 -> 2026-03-10
Context: short iteration cycle to compare small-model quant profiles and light-weight KV caching/batching heuristics. Goal is a reproducible micro-benchmark I can re-run before larger perf runs.

---
Summary notes (top-line):
- q4 quant profiles give big throughput wins on short sequences but can worsen tail latency unless batching/worker warmup is tuned.
- KV caching + small batching gave the largest cost reduction for multi-turn workloads (observed ~60% lower token cost in R3).
- Prewarm and kernel scheduling are major sources of variance for p95; need deterministic prewarm script.

---
Quick table (human-readable, not canonical CSV):
| run | config        | batch | seq | tokens/sec | median_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k | notes                          |
| R1  | fp16 baseline | 1     | 128 | 420        | 23        | 75    | $0.012      | cold start, no KV cache        |
| R2  | q4_0          | 1     | 128 | 610        | 16        | 90    | $0.008      | median up, p95 worse (jit)     |
| R3  | q4_kv_cache   | 4     | 512 | 1820       | 18        | 60    | $0.005      | batching + KV cache (multi-turn)|
| R4  | q4_kv_prewarm | 4     | 512 | 1700       | 17        | 48    | $0.0052     | prewarm attempt with staggered |

Notes on table: sequences measured are tokens generated per second for inference only (excl. tokenization). cost_per_1k is rough run-time compute cost estimate using on-demand GPU pricing; normalize later.

---
Raw observations / micro-postmortem:
- R2 p95 degraded likely due to kernel scheduling and fallback to slower matmul path on some token lengths. Seen on two different workers but not all.
- Warmup: sending 8 short warmup requests reduces p95 variance substantially on the same worker (baseline warmup script currently in /home/lucas/scratch/warmup.sh).
- Memory: quant load is cheaper but model load sometimes fails due to fragmentation (OOM in quant->torch conversion). Add retry with smaller chunk loads.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Re-run R2 with deterministic thread pinning and kernel overrides (ticket: INF-4242).
- [ ] Add continuous-batcher flag to runtime and test with batch cutoff 16ms.
- [ ] Collect nvprof traces for R2 vs R3 and attach to run folder /tmp/run-profiles/session-2026-03-10.
- [ ] Write short how-to (2 paragraphs) for reproducing microbench; share in #eng-applied-ml.

Open questions (notes to self):
- How consistent are q4 gains across hardware families? schedule quick test on A100 and g5 (TBD).
- Is p95 regression from q4 deterministic by sequence length or content? need per-seq-length breakdown.
- Can we exploit mixed precision (q4 + fp16 for attention) to balance tail? quick experiment idea: q4 for FFN, fp16 for attention.

Linked quick references:
- Linear: INF-4237 (compare quant profiles)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/912 (local kernel tweaks)
- Slack: #inference-kernels (see thread around 2026-02-26)

Short run log (timestamps):
2026-02-25 — R1 baseline (fp16)
2026-02-26 — R2 q4 quick (noted p95 jitter)
2026-03-01 — R3 batch+kv test (best cost so far)
2026-03-08 — R4 prewarm attempt (partial success, one worker failed to prewarm -> model load OOM)

Error snippets (copied):
[MODEL LOAD ERROR] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at 0x7f... during quant->allocate phase. stack: model_loader.cpp:142
Action: retry with smaller num-chunks=8 instead of default 4.

Perf debugging notes:
- Use perf markers in runtime around kernel launch (RUNTIME_MARKER_K) to correlate host->device latency.
- Collect worker logs with LOG_LEVEL=debug and tag by run-id (run-id format: lucas-YYYYMMDD-R#).

Next steps (practical):
1) Stabilize prewarm script and re-run R4 with staged preloads.
2) Add lightweight per-seq-length breakdown to microbench harness.
3) If reproducible, draft short note and propose a small kernel scheduling tweak in runtime (link to PR above).

Notes to self: keep this file lightweight — copy findings into a more formal doc if we want to surface to product or infra. For now, this is my personal quick-run ledger.

---
Appendix (commands I ran):
# small-run template
python tools/microbench.py --model t5-small-7b --profile q4_0 --batch 1 --seq 128 --warmup 8 --run-id lucas-20260225-r1

# collect traces
python infra/collect_traces.py --run-id lucas-20260301-r3 --out /tmp/run-profiles/session-2026-03-01

End of scratchsheet.
